card_rules.consensus: Pool as above, unplaced outlets included in counts and shown beside the bars. (1) The claim term: lead.claim.terms (the normaliser's whole-word count of the claim's titled headlines), a count card with the rung bars and the unplaced beside them. (2) Quoted phrases: every span inside quotation marks in a pool headline, three words or more, compared lowercased with curly quotes straightened; a span carried by placed outlets on three or more rungs is a consensus card showing, per rung, the earliest headline that carries it. Nothing else becomes a consensus card.
card_rules.divergence: Pool: the claim's titled headlines from placed outlets. For each fixed question, a headline is asked only if it names the people the question is about; words the headline attributes to someone else (a modal plus 'blame' and what follows, up to 'for' or punctuation) are set aside; its answers are the patterns the rest matches (case-insensitive, whole words; synonyms of one answer count as one). A pair qualifies when its two answer sets share nothing. Of the qualifying pairs, take the one whose rungs are farthest apart; then the pair whose earlier headline was published first; then the later; then ledger order. Show the pair left rung first. A question with no qualifying pair has no card.

parts.title: The Echo
parts.as_of_basis: The vote was cast on Tuesday 4 November 1952; the horizon is noon in Washington the next day. The result is known inside it from Stevenson's concession as the New York Times printed it that morning (src-stevenson-19521105), so the Echo may say who won the presidency and nothing more. Official counts (the electors' votes of December 1952, the Clerk's 1953 statistics) are later records and are never shown as known at the horizon. Truman's own statement of 5 November is not used: its hour is not shown.
parts.picked_after_week_known: This Echo was picked on 2026-11-12, after week 33's lead was known, because the pre-registered echo bank (24 echoes tagged by mechanism before any week's news, bible section k) has not yet been built.

device.reason: The past has no outlet measurement (grey bars only, bible c); balance is carried by period perspectives from both parties in their own words (Truman and Stevenson for the governing party, Eisenhower for the opposition), Truman's own counter-view included, and three period documents (E1).

fit_gap: Truman gave no reason tied to Korea when he withdrew; his 29 March words are used only for the withdrawal.
The New Hampshire vote is a preference poll inside one party in one state, not a national election.
Congress is not in the mechanism sentence: the 1952 House and Senate majorities were not read from a primary source in this session, and they were settled in the days after the vote.
No leader of the governing party names the war as the reason for the loss inside the horizon (the week's lead has one); none is held.

Truman's own address of 14 June 1951 says controls would be needed even if the fighting in Korea stopped tomorrow: the war is not, in his words, the only cause of the controls. The Echo reads that line (period_perspectives[0].counter).
outside_horizon: the electors' votes of 15 December 1952 and the Clerk's printed counts
parts.windows: every Echo search and item window ends on or before 1952-11-05T12:00:00-05:00

no_bridge.word_rule: Bare surnames that are also 1952 words or names are flagged only in full: 'Troy Jackson' (the Jefferson-Jackson Day Dinner is the 1952 event's own name), 'Susan Collins'; 'Miller', 'Wiles', 'Slotkin', 'Mamdani', 'Eisenkot' and 'Tajani' are flagged bare.
no_bridge.ruling: Founder's ruling (chat 2026-11-12, asked directly): the 1952 party names 'Democratic' and 'Republican' are allowed in the Echo as institutions; no person or event from this week's news may appear. 'GOP' and this week's persons and places stay flagged.
no_bridge.also: no 'like today', 'just as', or any sentence pointing at the week, in either direction (bible e)

reader.text: This is the problem of inflation and high prices.
